source_title: Daler Mehndi row: 'I want the truth to come out'; Maninder Buttar seeks full recording of 2019 show, deni - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Punjabi singer Maninder Buttar has spoken out against remarks allegedly made by Uttarakhand minister Subodh Uniyal during a confrontation with singer Daler Mehndi at a public event. Maninder has asked the minister to release the complete recording of his 2019 performance in Uttarakhand. He said the footage would help establish what happened and allow people to judge the incident independently.The controversy began earlier this month at the Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair in New Tehri. Daler Mehndi was performing at the event when Subodh Uniyal reportedly questioned his singing and accused him of being intoxicated. The minister also referred to Maninder's earlier visit to the state, making allegations about his behaviour during that performance.Subodh Uniyal's remarks bring Maninder Buttar into controversyDuring the exchange with Daler Mehndi, Subodh Uniyal reportedly referred to Maninder's previous performance and made a remark involving the singer's father. He was allegedly heard saying in Hindi, âYahaan aapse pehle Maninder Buttar pit ke gaya thaâ¦ aur itna pita tha ki uska baap bhi dobara nahi aa sakta yahaan pe."The comments prompted Maninder to address the matter during an Instagram Live session on Monday. The singer expressed disappointment over the alleged remarks and requested that the minister make the original footage public.Maninder Buttar recalls his 2019 Uttarakhand performanceManinder said he had travelled to Uttarakhand in 2019 and performed for more than an hour. He also recalled that Subodh Uniyal had joined him on stage and honoured him with a traditional Pahadi cap. According to the singer, he continued performing while wearing the cap.âI want the truth to come out. I respectfully request the Honâble Minister to upload the complete recording of that show so that everyone can see what actually happened and judge for themselves if I did anything wrong," Maninder said.The singer maintained that the recording would help clarify the circumstances surrounding the allegations. He wants the public to assess the footage rather than rely solely on claims made during the recent controversy.Maninder Buttar denies misconduct and alcohol useManinder also addressed the personal allegations, stating that he had always tried to treat people with respect. I have never intentionally hurt anyoneâs feelings, never indulged in any kind of misconduct, and have always tried to maintain my dignity and respect for others. I was genuinely shocked when I came to know that such things had been said about me and my father," he said.The singer further denied performing under the influence of alcohol or any other intoxicating substance. He explained that he had always taken his professional responsibilities seriously and preferred to keep his family away from public controversies.âI am a small artist, and I have always tried to keep my family away from controversies like these. I have never performed under the influence of alcohol or any intoxicating substance, and I have always taken my work and my responsibilities seriously. All I ask is for the complete, unedited recording of that show to be made public. Let people watch it, understand what really happened, and decide for themselves who is right and who is wrong," he added.Mika Singh backs Daler Mehndi and seeks an apologyMeanwhile, Mika Singh has defended Daler Mehndi against the allegations surrounding his performance. Mika said the singer had been unwell for the past two years and was still recovering. These days, many performers use backing tracks, but nobody questions them in the same way," Mika said, as reported by News 18.Mika also revealed that Daler Mehndi had asked him to drop the matter after contacting him.
